no_condition.why: NO BAR EXISTS. The trigger is 'when sizing the expected dominant-move magnitude', which is every day, and the call is an explicit instruction NOT to act ('CANDIDATE correction ONLY... Do NOT globally rescale'), deferring the actual sort to magnitude.catalyst_condition_sort. The play's own health field says the same in its own words. The only numbers in the record are five realized per-day forecast errors (guess vs actual), which are OUTCOMES logged after the fact, not a pre-decision quantity that can be read at the open and compared to a threshold. Turning a residual log into a bar would be manufacturing one.

QUANTITIES UNSERVED AND NO THRESHOLD WRITTEN. The read is 'the running (roll-clean) path at a cum-EXTREME + a counter-move in the old swing's LAST 1-2 days + last-hour momentum into the seam'. All three are price-path content and none is in the vocabulary: there is no cum-from-anchor, no running-extreme, no last-hour-direction field. vol_regime.n0_prev_net is the prior SESSION's own net, which is a different quantity from 'a counter-move in the old swing's last 1-2 days measured against the running extreme' - naming it would be exactly the nearest-looking-name error. Separately the play states no number at all: 'a stretched swing' and 'cum-extreme' are qualitative descriptors, so even with the field served there would be nothing to write. The play's health field records a fire rate of 0 of 60 days on the current architecture for this reason.

BAR IS REAL BUT NAMES AN UNSERVED QUANTITY. The trigger carries two numeric bars - swing AGE (<=3 young / >=4 mature, in sessions since the swing turned) and a materiality bar of '>= ~$300 beyond the prior extreme close'. Neither operand is served: the vocabulary has no swing-age or chain-age field (squeeze_watch.sessions_since_prompt_expiry counts contract expiries, not swing turns) and no close-vs-running-extreme field. vol_regime.n0_prev_net is a session net, not a close measured against the running extreme, so it cannot carry the $300 bar. The play's own health field records that specialists stand it down day after day in the blind because 'chain age and cum-from-anchor are price content the mask removes'. The s101_6 expiry-day form appended in legacy_notes does reference stranded premium (contract_structure.calendar_front_next_spread), but that arm states no threshold and its own brain_action assigns it to structure.squeeze_unwind, not to this play's trigger.

BAR IS REAL BUT NAMES AN UNSERVED QUANTITY. The bar is a retrace fraction of the swing (>=~75%, softened to >=~70%) measured against the swing's origin/consolidation SHELF PRICE. Both operands are price-path content and neither is served: there is no retrace-fraction, no cum-from-anchor, and no swing-origin price level anywhere in the vocabulary. The shelf is explicitly 'a zone, not a tick', so even the reference level is not a single served number. The play's health field states it directly - refine-only in the modern architecture, and the one time a blind fired it, it fired against a shelf that had already broken.

EVERY ARM'S OPERAND IS UNSERVED, INCLUDING THE ONE THE BAR IS MEASURED AGAINST. The ARM needs swing amplitude as a ratio of 'the season's prior largest swing' (>=~1.5-2x), run length in sessions (>=~9), and a close >=~30% off the intraday extreme. The CONFIRM needs C1 (the counter day's net breaking its condition-class counter band by >=~1.5x), C2 (old-direction leg continuation <=~15% and big legs <=~1/3 alive), C3 (a sequencing rule - 'printed, never front-run' - which carries no bar at all), and C4 (the direction the next print delivers). None of swing amplitude, run length, close-off-extreme, leg-continuation rate or arbiter-print direction is served. vol_regime.n0_prev_net does serve a prior-session net, but C1's threshold is a 1.5x RATIO against a condition-class counter-band table that the play's own health field says 'are not served as a numeric table anywhere - each specialist re-derives them', so there is no reference value to write and any absolute dollar figure would be invented. The play's health field is unambiguous: C1 is 'permanently UNKNOWN - never true, never false' on the architecture that now runs.

THE NUMBERS ARE OUTPUTS, NOT A CONDITION. Every figure in this play is an expected day-net dollar band (-2400..-2900, -1800..-4000, +800..+1900, and so on) - i.e. the play's emission, not a quantity read at the open and compared to a threshold. Its actual gating condition is 'after a confirmed polarity flip (crash chain / basing)', which is structure.chain_polarity_flip's output and is itself unserved, and the six condition classes ('flip-confirm + chained crash', 'print-liquidity crash', 'exhausted-leg bounce', 'liquidation flush', ...) are day-class descriptors with no served quantity behind them. Writing any of these dollar bands as a state_path threshold would assert that the forecaster can read its own answer at the open.

BAR IS REAL BUT NAMES AN UNSERVED QUANTITY. The arming quantity is the prior day's INTRADAY counter-chain spike measured against its close - 'closes >=~60% off the counter extreme' - which is intraday price-path content. The vocabulary carries no intraday peak, close, or round-trip fraction; vol_regime.n0_prev_range and n0_prev_net give a prior session's high-low range and net, from which a signed, polarity-relative peak-to-close round-trip cannot be recovered. The declared FLOW substitute (a phase_signed_flow reversal within the session) is a genuinely different quantity, is not served either (only the session-level tape_conditions.session_signed_flow is, and a session aggregate cannot express an intraday round-trip), and one of the two specialists who used it withdrew it in writing with an explicit 'do not bank this'. The play's own health field records the deeper problem: in blind mode the fade percentage was taken off the forecaster's own GUESSED curve, so 'this play does not have an input; it has a mirror'.
